drhp.business: RIR Power Electronics manufactures low- and high-power semiconductor devices (diodes, thyristors, thyristor modules and bridge rectifiers), processing semiconductor chips from 28 mm to 125 mm in diameter at its Halol, Gujarat facility. It also makes power electronic equipment such as rectifiers, battery chargers, high-power stacks and rectifier panels, plus rectifier systems for green hydrogen electrolysis. Customers are in defence, aerospace, railways and industrial applications, and the company is developing next-generation Silicon Carbide (SiC) power devices.

drhp.expansion: The company is setting up a Silicon Carbide (SiC) plant in Odisha (6,186 million rupees), described as 'a first of its kind in India', with help from the Odisha state government incentive scheme. The plant is meant to build an ecosystem through vertical integration, secure the supply chain and cut India's dependence on imported SiC components. During FY26, capex was incurred at the new Odisha plant to make SiC wafers and devices. In the same year the company sold 100% of its subsidiary Visicon Power Electronics Private Limited (SiC wafers and power devices via an epitaxial process) to Silicon Power Corporation, U.S.A.; Visicon ceased to be a subsidiary w.e.f. 26 July 2025. This bundle states no commissioning timeline.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- More electric vehicles, renewable energy, smart grids, localisation, and investment in railways, defence and industrial automation are named as demand drivers
- Demand for wide-bandgap technologies such as Silicon Carbide is said to offer meaningful growth potential
- Data centres, AI platforms and digital ecosystems need high power quality and reliability, which management says will drive demand for power electronics
- Government semiconductor policy (India Semiconductor Mission 2.0) is backing ecosystem build-out in fabrication, packaging and power semiconductors
- FY26 saw moderate demand across Semiconductor Devices, High Power Equipment and Exports. Management attributes the temporary moderation to customer-led scheduling changes, the new labour codes and higher raw-material consumption costs
- Management expects the previous year's positive trend to continue in FY 2026-27
- The order backlog is about ₹17 crore. Management says it gives revenue visibility for the coming quarters
- The first overseas order, for 5 kV 125-mm press-pack SCR thyristors, will be executed in phases through the end of 2026

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The company is setting up a Silicon Carbide (SiC) plant in Odisha (6,186 million rupees), described as 'a first of its kind in India', with help from the Odisha state government incentive scheme. The plant is meant to build an ecosystem through vertical integration, secure the supply chain and cut India's dependence on imported SiC components. During FY26, capex was incurred at the new Odisha plant to make SiC wafers and devices. In the same year the company sold 100% of its subsidiary Visicon Power Electronics Private Limited (SiC wafers and power devices via an epitaxial process) to Silicon Power Corporation, U.S.A.; Visicon ceased to be a subsidiary w.e.f. 26 July 2025. This bundle states no commissioning timeline.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- licence/regulatory: approved railway vendor status — evidence: the AR lists 'RDSO Approval – Part One Supplier to Indian Railways' among its industry certifications
- integration: in-house device fabrication from silicon processing to finished systems — evidence: the Halol plant runs wafer diffusion, vacuum evaporation, alloying, welding and electroplating, and processes semiconductor chips from 28 mm to 125 mm in diameter; the company also makes power equipment (rectifiers, battery chargers, high-power stacks)
- technology: high-power device capability qualified in defence and export use — evidence: developed a 25 kV–120 kA capacitor-discharge semiconductor switch during the year; 125 mm Light Silicon Sandwich device for an electromagnetic railgun; first overseas order for 5 kV 125-mm press-pack SCR thyristors; the Chairman reports 'successful qualification and deployment of high-power semiconductor solutions for defence applications'
- technology: domestic Silicon Carbide (SiC) power-device manufacturing — evidence: SiC facility in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, with cleanroom construction completed and plant-and-machinery installation underway; epitaxial wafer production targeted to start in Q3 FY27; described as 'a first of its kind in India' [planned] — against it: during FY26 the company sold 100% of its SiC-epitaxy subsidiary Visicon Power Electronics Private Limited to Silicon Power Corporation, U.S.A.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Build domestic Silicon Carbide (SiC) semiconductor manufacturing at the Bhubaneswar, Odisha facility, aligned with Make in India, to reduce India's reliance on imported SiC components
- Grow presence in railways, defence, renewable energy, grid infrastructure and other critical applications
- Establish itself as a domestic technology partner for defence through qualified high-power semiconductor solutions
- Keep product innovation (for example, high-energy pulse-power switches) central to growth and widen the technology-led product portfolio
- Expand exports, starting with the first overseas order for 5 kV SCR thyristors
- FY27 focus: execution, technology advancement and operational efficiency

one-line thesis: RIR delivered 36% YoY revenue growth and 77% EBITDA growth in Q2FY26, driven by strong demand in railways, defense, and renewables, while making concrete progress on its 618-crore SiC ecosystem — with Phase 1 EPI reactor commissioning slated for January 2026 and NSE listing by March 2026, positioning it as India’s first domestic SiC wafer producer.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +36% YoY (₹25.64cr vs ₹18.82cr); EBITDA: +77% YoY (₹4.36cr vs ₹2.46cr), margin expanded 392 bps to 17.01%; PAT: +105% YoY (₹3.15cr vs ₹1.53cr), normalized PAT excludes one-off government grant recognition; Order book: Not disclosed; Net debt: Net cash position improving, with ₹85cr equity raised and debt negotiations ongoing for Phase 1
guidance: Revenue growth: Targeting ₹8-10cr from EPI in FY26, ₹60cr+ in FY27; Margin: Expecting gradual improvement to 18-20% by FY27; Order inflow: LOIs from Alpha Omega, ST Micro, Microchip; Capex/commissioning: ₹106cr for EPI phase (Jan 2026 commissioning), ₹100cr for packaging, full 618cr ecosystem by FY28
order book & pipeline: Not disclosed; LOIs secured from Alpha Omega Semiconductor, ST Microelectronics, Microchip for SiC EPI wafers
segment / subsidiary detail: SiC EPI wafer production: 150mm line, 4000 wafers/month capacity; Target thickness: 30-180 microns (3.3kV-20kV range); Current output: 10,000 devices shipped to Indian Navy (Q2FY26) via Taiwan contract manufacturer; Revenue mix: 65% export, 35% domestic; Input cost: $250/substrate; Selling price: $800 (50um) to $1500 (180um); Yield: 85% target
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into 3.3kV+ IGBTs for Indian Railways and HVDC grids; Potential licensing of IP to domestic OEMs; Export market penetration via LOIs with global players; Future 200mm readiness (long-term, post-FY28)
margins & cost dynamics: Margin expansion driven by higher-value SiC EPI mix (vs legacy silicon devices), improved operational discipline, and lower outsourced manufacturing costs; Cost pressure from global transformer lead times (33kV to 1MW step-down) delaying power supply to Bhubaneswar fab; EPI gross margin expected to exceed 60% at scale
capex / expansion: Total capex: ₹618cr; Phase 1 (EPI + Packaging): ₹225cr (₹106cr EPI, ₹100cr packaging, ₹19cr ancillary); Phase 2 (Device Fab): ₹400cr; FY26 capex: ₹68cr spent + ₹50cr planned; Funding: ₹85cr equity (preferential issue), ₹30cr debt planned for Phase 1; Odisha govt grant: ₹32.56cr received (50% of Phase 1), ₹26cr deposited in Nov 2025
capital allocation: Priority: Fund Phase 1 EPI/packaging (₹225cr) via equity (₹85cr done) + debt (₹30cr target); Next: Secure ₹200cr Odisha grant for Phase 2 (device fab); Explore strategic investor infusion for long-term capex; NSE listing to unlock valuation and reduce equity dilution
risks & watch-items: Power supply delay to Bhubaneswar fab (33kV to 1MW transformer lead time); Delay in MD appointment (targeted by Dec 2025); Execution risk in achieving 85% EPI yield; Geopolitical disruption in Taiwan contract manufacturing; Debt funding delays; Competition from subsidized Chinese SiC players
management quality / tone: Confident, technically detailed, and execution-focused; Management emphasizes India’s first-mover advantage in medium/high-voltage SiC; Acknowledges execution risks but highlights strong academic partnerships (TIFR, IITs) and government support; Tone on NSE listing and MD appointment is urgent but non-committal on exact dates
non-obvious takeaways: RIR is already shipping qualified SiC devices to Indian Navy using Taiwan-manufactured wafers — proving commercial viability before domestic fab is live; The company’s focus on 3.3kV+ (not EV-focused 1200V) avoids direct competition with Chinese giants; Academic partnerships (TIFR, IITs) are being leveraged for process know-how, not just funding

outlook.body: Revenue growth: Targeting ₹8-10cr from EPI in FY26, ₹60cr+ in FY27; Margin: Expecting gradual improvement to 18-20% by FY27; Order inflow: LOIs from Alpha Omega, ST Micro, Microchip; Capex/commissioning: ₹106cr for EPI phase (Jan 2026 commissioning), ₹100cr for packaging, full 618cr ecosystem by FY28
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not disclosed; LOIs secured from Alpha Omega Semiconductor, ST Microelectronics, Microchip for SiC EPI wafers
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into 3.3kV+ IGBTs for Indian Railways and HVDC grids; Potential licensing of IP to domestic OEMs; Export market penetration via LOIs with global players; Future 200mm readiness (long-term, post-FY28)
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: RIR delivered 36% YoY revenue growth and 77% EBITDA growth in Q2FY26, driven by strong demand in railways, defense, and renewables, while making concrete progress on its 618-crore SiC ecosystem — with Phase 1 EPI reactor commissioning slated for January 2026 and NSE listing by March 2026, positioning it as India’s first domestic SiC wafer producer.

hero.oneLiner: RIR Power Electronics describes itself as India's only manufacturer of silicon-based power semiconductor devices, making thyristors, diodes, modules and power equipment and building a Silicon Carbide (SiC) device facility in Odisha.
